PILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City MAYOR DENISA R. REPIZO Municipality of Magdiwang Province of Romblon Dear Mayor Repizo: http: //www dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. S. 201B This has reference to your letter dated 15 February 2018 requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following issues enumerated and quoted here in verbatim, to wit: I. Whether any interested person/taxpayer may be allowed to access and be issued copy of PDS of a government employee; and 2. Ifthe same is not absolute, what information in the PDS may be accessed by or given to the public? Given that the issues are interrelated, they shall be answered in one discussion. The right of the people to information on matters of public concern has been enshrined in our Constitution, particularly in Section 7, Article III. Such right has been echoed by Section 3 of Executive Order (EO) No. 02, series Of 20161, which provides: "SECTION 3. Access to information. Every Filipino shall have access to information, official records, public records and to documents and papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, as well as to government research data used as basis for policy development. ' However, the exercise of the right to information on matters of public concern is not absolute. Section 4 of the aforementioned EO provides the exceptions: 'SECTION 4. Exception. Access to information shall be denied when the information falls under any of the exceptions enshrined in the Constitution, existing law or jurisprudence. " Entitled, "Operationalizing in the Executive Branch the People's Constitutional Right to Information and the State Policies to Full Public Disclosure and Transparency in the Public Service and Providing Guidelines Therefor.

The Department of Justice and the Office of the Solicitor General are hereby directed to prepare an inventory of such exceptions and submit the same to the Office of the President within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of effectivity of this Order. " In addition, a Memorandum from the Executive Secretary dated 24 November 2016 provides for the inventory of Exceptions to EO No. 2. Pertinent to your query, i.e. personnel records, would fall under the fourth (4th) exception, indicated herein as follows: "4. Information deemed confidential for the protection Of the privacy of persons and certain individuals such as minors, victims OT crimes, or the accused. These include: a. Information of a personal nature where disålosure would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of perynal privacy?, personal information or records3, including sensitive personal information4, birth records', school record', or medical or health records7,• XXX xxv However, personal information may be disclosed to the extent that the requested information is shown to be a matter of public concern or interest, shall not meddle with or disturb the private life or family relations of the individual and is not prohibited by any law or regulation. Any disclosure of personal information shall be in accordance with the principles of transparency, legitimate purpose and proportionality. " 2 Section 3(e), Rule IV of the Rules on the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (CCESPOE). 3 Section of DPA provides that, "Personal information "refers to any information whether recorded in a material form or not, from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained by the entity holding the information, or when put together with other information would directly and certainly identify an individual. 4 Section 3(1) of DPA provides that, "Sensitive personal information "refers to personal information: (1) About an individual's race, ethnic origin, marital status, age, color, and religious, philosophical or political affiliations; (2) About an individual's health, education, genetic or sexual life ofa person, the disposal of such proceedings, or the sentence of any courr in such proceedings; (3) Issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual which includes, but not limited to, social security numbers, previous or cm-rent health records, licenses or its denials, suspension or revocation, and tax returns; and (4) Specifically established by an executive order or an act of Congress to be kept classified. 5 Article 7 of PD No. 603, otherwise known as "The Child and Youth Welfare Code 6 Section 9(4) of Batas Pambansa (BP) mg. 232, otherwise known as the "Education Act of 1982" 7 Section 3(1) of the DPA

The aforementioned Memorandum, citing Section 4 of Republic Act (RA) NO. 10173, otherwise known as the "Data Privacy Act of 2012" (DPA), also provides that the disclosure of personal information is allowed if it pertains to any individual who is or was an officer or employee of a government institution and the query relates to or in connection with the position or functions of the said individual, including: 1. The fact that the individual is or was an officer or employee of the government institution; 2. The title, business address, and office telephone number of the individual:; 3. The classification, salary range and responsibilities of the position held by the individual; and 4. The name of the individual on a document prepared by the individual in the course of employment with the government. Given the above discussions, although a PDS is a public document8 that contains information pertaining to that employee or official, including his or her personal background, qualifications and eligibility9, however it does not mean that a copy and the contents of which if for public consumption and can be readily be accessed by anyone upon mere request. A government agency or office, acting as the proper custodian of such document, may provide certain rules or a set of criteria against which a request for said document shall be measured or assessed. Since such document contains sensitive and confidential matters, the concerned government office or agency has the obligation to regulate access to or disclosure of the same. Although a person has the right to information on matters Of public concern, however such right must be balanced and should also respect an individual's right to privacy including those confidential in nature. The latin maxim, sic utere tuo ut alienum non laedas or to exercise such a right in such a way that you do not injure other people's right/property, is applicable in this case. Thus, if an individual would request access to the PDS of a government employee, said individual may be granted access to such document provided that the information requested falls under Section 4 of the DPA and such request complies with the rules and regulations set forth by the concerned agency or office. 8 Under Section 19, Rule 1320fthe Rules of Court, the following are public documents: (a) The written official acts, or records of the official acts of the sovereign authority, official bodies and tribunals, and public officers, whether of the Philippines, or ofa foreign country; (b) Documents acknowledge before a notary public except last wills and testaments; and (c) Public records, kept in the Philippines, of private documents required bylaw to be entered therein. 9Advincu1a vs. Dicen. G.R. No. 162403. 16 d5R

It is also noteworthy to mention that the National Privacy Commission (NPC) Advisory NO. 2017-02, dated 03 April 201710, provides for its recommendations when resolving a pending request for access to a PDS. In the said NPC Advisory, it provides that a government agency or office, when granting access to a government employee's PDS must consider the following: "l. the information requested falls under matters of public concern; 2. the individual requesting Tor personal data has declared an d specified the purpose of his or her request; 3. the declared and specified purpose is not contrary to morals, and public policy; and 4. the personal data requested is necessary to the declared, specified, and legitimate purpose. At the same time, the requesting party is obliged to use the data obtained only for the purpose declared at the time of making of the request. The individual must also commit to complying the provisions of the DPA. " With these at hand, we hope that the Department has enlightened you on the ma tter. cc: Very truly yours, By Authority of the Sec etary: C.
